packs.title: Stone, Art and Sea
packs.promise: Explore a market and two museums, then make separate Marble Mountains and Son Tra coastal outings.

q.s: Find how a working market displays, portions and carries goods.
st: Follow one open customer aisle through the dry-goods and food trading areas without entering preparation or storage spaces.
Find an example of goods displayed for comparison, an example divided into portions, and an example packaged to carry away. Observe from the customer side without handling anything.
Make a three-part field note: describe each arrangement and explain which job its container or layout does.
Choose one detail you would miss in a quick shopping visit and add it to your note.

q.s: Turn a gallery arrangement into your own small composition.
st: Enter with a valid ticket and choose one painting or graphic work in an open visitor display.
Look for a large shape, a smaller counterweight and the space between them. Keep those as your observations rather than guessing what the artist intended.
After leaving the galleries, create an original arrangement using three different shapes of your own. A written layout describing their placement works equally well.
Add a short note explaining one balance you borrowed and one choice you changed.

q.s: Make two connected panels from a coastal pavement.
st: Find an open public paved position on the beach side near Hoang Ke Viem, away from crossings and service access.
Look toward the shore, then turn toward the city edge: compare the long horizon with the road, palms and buildings you can actually see.
Create two linked panels, one for shore and one for street. Draw them or describe their lines and sounds in writing.
Carry one repeated shape or word across both panels and explain how it changes between the two views.

packs.title: Along the Han
packs.promise: Explore the Han River’s western city edge and a connected cross-river afternoon.

q.s: Collect evidence of nature, boats and urban life in the new museum.
st: Enter with a valid ticket and follow current visitor directions to the open nature, maritime and city-life displays.
Choose an available object or model in each of those themes: something showing the natural setting, a boat or maritime practice, and a detail of how people made the city work.
Collect a visible material or shape detail for each, and one relevant label fact where available.
Write a short connection between the three, clearly separating what you saw from what a label told you.

q.s: Make an original arrangement from Han Market’s trading colours.
st: Observe an open customer-side textile or packaged dry-goods display without touching goods or blocking customers.
Choose two contrasting colours and one repeated fold, stripe or package shape that you actually see.
After stepping clear of trading circulation, arrange those elements in an original patchwork drawing or a written description of a small pattern.
Explain which part came from observation and which arrangement you invented.

q.s: Rest on the public park path beneath a changing lattice view.
st: Choose a clear ordinary public paved park position with a view of the white lattice canopy, standing or using an available lawful public seat.
Pause for two minutes. Look through one opening in the lattice, then at the solid ground and garden around you.
Write one sentence about how the open pattern changes your view and one about where the river walk has brought you.
